title: Silicon Valley: Ecosystem, Transition, and Regional Costs
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: 四つの原文段落と全九つの学習対象を保持し、元の記述問題を英語四択へ変換しました。

passages.text:
Silicon Valley, the southern part of the San Francisco Bay Area, is often represented by a garage and a gifted founder. That image captures experimentation but hides an ecosystem. Federal research and defense procurement created demanding early markets; universities trained engineers and connected research to firms; semiconductor companies developed production knowledge; investors financed uncertain growth; and mobile workers carried skills between organizations.

Once these elements interacted, clustering could reinforce itself. A new firm could find specialized lawyers, suppliers, managers, and engineers nearby. Successful employees could become investors or founders, while failure did not always end a career. Yet proximity was never the whole system. Chip fabrication, mineral extraction, assembly, data centers, and consumer markets stretched across regions and countries. The celebrated address depended on a much wider geography of labor and infrastructure.

The cluster also changed. Leadership moved from electronic components toward personal computing, software, internet services, mobile platforms, and artificial intelligence. This does not mean each stage replaced the previous one completely. Older capabilities, firms, and capital were recombined. Nor does the persistence of the name prove that every innovative activity remains local; distributed teams and global supply chains complicate the boundary of the region.

Finally, innovation success is not identical to regional well-being. High wages and firm growth can coexist with expensive housing, long commutes, unequal access to schools and services, labor segmentation, and environmental burdens. Patent counts and investment flows measure important outputs, not the complete social result. To evaluate a technology region, we should ask not only what it invents, but who can remain there, who performs less visible work, and where the costs are placed.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: One founder and one garage created the entire technology region.

options.label: B
options.text: The region should be understood as an evolving ecosystem whose benefits and costs extend beyond its borders.

options.label: C
options.text: All semiconductor production has always remained local.

options.label: D
options.text: High patent counts prove equal regional well-being.

questions.answer: 正解：B。本文は公共調達、大学、企業、資本、人材と広域供給網が変化しながら相互作用する生態系として描き、成果と費用の分配も評価します。A・C・Dは単独英雄・地域内完結・成果の均等分配へ単純化します。

questions.prompt: Which list contains four institutions or actors that helped form the cluster?

options.label: A
options.text: Federal research and defense procurement, universities, semiconductor firms, and investors

options.label: B
options.text: Only one garage, one founder, one patent, and one local customer

options.label: C
options.text: Housing shortages, long commutes, school inequality, and waste alone

options.label: D
options.text: Identical public funding, immobile workers, no suppliers, and no early markets

questions.answer: 正解：A。本文は連邦研究・防衛調達、大学、半導体企業、投資家に加え、組織間を移る技術者・労働者を形成要因として挙げます。B～Dは生態系の相互依存を消しています。

questions.prompt: The phrase “reinforce itself” is closest in meaning to

options.label: A
options.text: existing advantages attract resources that create further advantages

options.label: B
options.text: every company receives identical public funding

options.label: C
options.text: geography becomes completely irrelevant

options.label: D
options.text: old technologies disappear at once

questions.answer: 正解：A。既存の集積が専門人材・供給者・資本を呼び、それが次の企業と優位を生む自己強化です。Bは資金の同一性を捏造し、Cはclusterと逆、Dは再結合を無視します。

questions.prompt: Why does the passage say that proximity was never the whole system?

options.label: A
options.text: Fabrication, mineral extraction, assembly, data centers, and markets extended across other regions and countries on which local firms depended.

options.label: B
options.text: Every stage of production and consumption occurred within one neighborhood.

options.label: C
options.text: Global labor and infrastructure had no relationship to the cluster.

options.label: D
options.text: Specialized workers and suppliers were absent from the region.

questions.answer: 正解：A。地域内の近接性は重要でも、製造、鉱物採掘、組立、データセンター、市場は他地域・他国へ広がり、その労働と設備に依存します。B～Dは広域地理を否定します。

questions.prompt: Why did each new industry stage not completely replace the earlier one?

options.label: A
options.text: Older firms, skills, capital, and production knowledge were retained and recombined in later stages.

options.label: B
options.text: Every earlier capability disappeared before personal computing began.

options.label: C
options.text: The region never changed beyond electronic components.

options.label: D
options.text: Distributed teams made accumulated local knowledge irrelevant.

questions.answer: 正解：A。旧段階で蓄積した企業、技能、資本、生産知識が次段階へ再利用・再結合され、一部は存続しました。Bは完全置換、Cは変化なし、Dは蓄積の役割を否定します。

questions.prompt: Which evaluation is supported by the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Patent counts are useless and should never be measured.

options.label: B
options.text: Investment alone proves that every resident benefits.

options.label: C
options.text: Innovation outputs are important but must be combined with distributional and regional indicators.

options.label: D
options.text: Housing has no relation to an innovation cluster.

questions.answer: 正解：C。特許や投資は重要なoutputですが、住宅費、通勤、教育・サービス、労働分断、環境負担と合わせる必要があります。Aは出力指標を否定しすぎ、B・Dは分配結果を無視します。

questions.prompt: Which set consists entirely of work or costs often placed outside the celebrated technology address?

options.label: A
options.text: Mineral extraction, chip fabrication, assembly, data-center operation, and waste burdens

options.label: B
options.text: Only founder speeches, local patents, and venture-capital announcements

options.label: C
options.text: No manufacturing, logistics, energy use, or environmental effects

options.label: D
options.text: Identical wages and services for every worker in every location

questions.answer: 正解：A。鉱物採掘、半導体製造、組立、データセンター、物流、廃棄物・環境負担は有名な所在地の外に置かれやすい仕事と費用です。B～Dは見えにくい依存を捉えません。

questions.prompt: What does the idea “Innovation has an address, but not a single author” imply?

options.label: A
options.text: A symbolic place may matter, but innovation depends on public funding, researchers, workers, suppliers, investors, and production across many locations.

options.label: B
options.text: The named region and one founder deserve all credit for every input and cost.

options.label: C
options.text: Geographic clustering has no effect whatsoever.

options.label: D
options.text: Less visible labor and infrastructure do not contribute to invention.

questions.answer: 正解：A。「革新には住所があるが、単独の著者はいない」。象徴的集積地を認めつつ、功績と依存を公的資金、研究者、労働者、供給者、他地域の生産へ分配して読みます。B～Dはガレージ神話を温存します。

questions.prompt: Which indicator set best evaluates the success of a technology region?

options.label: A
options.text: Innovation and firm outcomes together with housing burden, commute time, school access, occupational pay gaps, resource use, and the locations of manufacturing and waste

options.label: B
options.text: Patent totals alone, with no information about residents or workers

options.label: C
options.text: Investment flows alone, assuming every benefit and cost remains local

options.label: D
options.text: Founder wealth while excluding contract workers, public services, and environmental burdens

questions.answer: 正解：A。特許、新企業、生産性波及、研究、人材移動と、所得別住宅負担、通勤、教育、賃金差、資源利用、製造・廃棄場所を区別して測ります。B～Dは技術出力を完全な社会成果と誤認します。
